_about: The executable engines presented by PURPOSE (communications/DESIGN_brief_deliverables.md §D). plain_name is the executive register; analysts/researchers see the engine name. Joined at runtime with the capability registry by src/dossier/catalog.py — an engine missing from the registry is dropped, never shown stale.

groups.title: Test a position
groups.purpose: what can be attacked, what accepting it commits you to

engines.use_when: know where an argument is strong and where it can be attacked — the hidden premises, the weak joints, who bears the burden of proof
engines.yields: claim-by-claim scorecard (claim · evidence · unstated premise · weak joint · attack)
engines.row_unit: one row per major claim

engines.use_when: know what you are really signing up for if you adopt a position, a framework, a pledge
engines.yields: ledger of explicit → implicit commitments, their conflicts, what depends on what, the practical "so what"
engines.row_unit: one row per commitment

engines.use_when: trace opposed positions, responses and unresolved limits without assuming every text resolves them
engines.yields: position, transition and remainder tables
engines.row_unit: one row per supported tension or transition

engines.use_when: test a supposition, the conditions it holds fixed and the strongest alternative route
engines.yields: supposition and dependency tables with conclusions that survive
engines.row_unit: one row per supposition or alternative

engines.use_when: know which "must / cannot / could" claims are real necessities and which are emphasis
engines.yields: inventory of necessity/possibility claims with their backing and confusions
engines.row_unit: one row per must/could/can't claim

engines.use_when: separate what a text says must, may or cannot happen and under which conditions
engines.yields: modal claims with speakers, scope, backing and examples
engines.row_unit: one row per scoped possibility or necessity claim

engines.use_when: explain documented choices through incentives, constraints and available alternatives
engines.yields: choice and constraint tables with supported explanations
engines.row_unit: one row per choice or constraint

groups.title: See the structure
groups.purpose: the template that repeats, the ideas that hold it up

engines.use_when: have several cases or texts and need the one template that repeats across them (and where each case departs from it)
engines.yields: the template's stages with every case mapped onto them; departures flagged
engines.row_unit: one row per case × stage

engines.use_when: know which ideas hold the whole thing up — remove it and the argument collapses
engines.yields: ranking of concepts by what depends on them; hub/bridge topology
engines.row_unit: one row per concept

engines.use_when: know what job each key term is doing (foundation, defence, bridge, conclusion) and where the argument is thin
engines.yields: term-by-job table + vulnerability points
engines.row_unit: one row per key term

engines.use_when: know which frameworks and lenses the material thinks with, and what each lets you see and not see
engines.yields: inventory of frameworks (where used · what it shows · what it hides · where it came from)
engines.row_unit: one row per framework

engines.use_when: test a comparison’s relevant similarities, defeating differences, criteria and alternatives
engines.yields: comparison audits and bounded conclusions
engines.row_unit: one row per comparison or supported criterion

engines.use_when: see how a text selects resources, combines mechanisms and bounds its contribution
engines.yields: construction and evidence tables retaining each distinct contribution
engines.row_unit: one row per input, construction move or evidential limit

engines.use_when: know the kinds of reasoning a text relies on (probabilistic, strategic, normative…) and how rigorously
engines.yields: inventory of reasoning forms with rigor notes
engines.row_unit: one row per reasoning form

engines.use_when: map the lenses, components and relations a text uses to explain its object
engines.yields: component–relation and application–limit tables
engines.row_unit: one row per component, relation or application

engines.use_when: two or more supplied cases (states, programmes, firms) must be answered on the same questions, case by case, with the differences that survive the evidence and the limits of the comparison
engines.yields: case × question matrix with anchored cells, per-case answers, comparison limits
engines.row_unit: one row per case answer or matrix cell

engines.use_when: compare how supplied sources answer shared questions and where their scope differs
engines.yields: shared-question reconciliation and source-attributed theme coverage
engines.row_unit: one row per aligned question or evidenced theme

engines.use_when: identify the actors, their interests and their documented ways of exercising influence
engines.yields: actor inventory and supported influence relations
engines.row_unit: one row per actor or influence relation

engines.use_when: follow who supplies, receives and controls resources, preserving amount and delivery status
engines.yields: resource inventory and distribution relations
engines.row_unit: one row per resource flow or control

engines.use_when: inventory named actors, organizations and projects with source-supported roles and aliases
engines.yields: entity register and relationship table
engines.row_unit: one row per entity or documented relation

groups.title: Follow the words
groups.purpose: how terms move, get captured, change meaning

engines.use_when: the same term appears across documents or years and you need to know how its meaning shifted
engines.yields: trajectory table (term · meaning in A · meaning in B · what changed · what it now licenses)
engines.row_unit: one row per term × document
engines.fit_note: ok on corpora; designed for prior/current work of one author

engines.use_when: trace how a text credits and uses borrowed ideas, and what actually changes across supplied works
engines.yields: borrowing and use tables with attribution and limits
engines.row_unit: one row per attributed use or supported change

engines.use_when: one concept is central and you need its whole neighbourhood — near-synonyms, opposites, boundary cases
engines.yields: field map for 3–5 concepts
engines.row_unit: one row per related term

engines.use_when: you have per-document concept readings and need one cross-document picture with a verdict
engines.yields: unified concept picture + convergence/divergence + verdict
engines.row_unit: one row per concept
engines.fit_note: synthesis pass; needs prior phases — only as the last step after a concept engine

engines.use_when: an author or organisation changed its line and you need to see how the change was managed (silent revision, reframing, disavowal)
engines.yields: tactic catalogue with evidence
engines.row_unit: one row per tactic instance
engines.fit_note: presumes the same author across time (e.g. successive annual reports); off for mixed-author bundles

engines.use_when: compare what the same concepts mean and do across supplied works
engines.yields: concept-by-work map with supported continuities and changes
engines.row_unit: one row per aligned concept

engines.use_when: see how supplied works present continuity, qualification and revision
engines.yields: position map and revision record with earlier qualifications
engines.row_unit: one row per supported relation between positions

engines.use_when: distinguish a term’s local senses, neighbors, contrasts and speakers
engines.yields: meaning and contrast inventories with separate evidence for each sense
engines.row_unit: one row per local sense or contrast

engines.use_when: see how a text uses images and comparisons to frame an idea
engines.yields: metaphor inventory and mappings with limits
engines.row_unit: one row per metaphor or mapping

engines.use_when: identify how a text classifies things and handles difficult or conditional membership
engines.yields: category inventory and boundary cases
engines.row_unit: one row per category or boundary case

groups.title: Read it properly
groups.purpose: what a text argues, how it is built, what it hides

engines.use_when: know what each document actually argues, how, and what it foregrounds or suppresses — and, as a last pass, one synthesis across the phases
engines.yields: per-document argument map (thesis · moves · evidence · what is suppressed · key vocabulary)
engines.row_unit: one row per document

engines.use_when: how the story is told matters — voice, arc, what the sequencing does to the reader
engines.yields: story-shape reading per document
engines.row_unit: one row per document

engines.use_when: know how the authors claim to know what they claim — methods, standpoint, self-awareness — before you rely on them
engines.yields: credibility grounding per document
engines.row_unit: one row per document

engines.use_when: know what had to be in place for this argument or practice to emerge, and what it forecloses
engines.yields: enabling/constraining conditions + paths not taken
engines.row_unit: one row per condition
engines.fit_note: designed around an author's prior work; usable at surface on a corpus

engines.use_when: a single long work (book, long report) needs a map of what each part does and depends on
engines.yields: chapter role map with dependencies and weak points
engines.row_unit: one row per chapter
engines.fit_note: single long work only; off for multi-paper bundles

engines.use_when: follow an exposition’s sequence, voices, time and qualifications
engines.yields: sequence and perspective maps suited to the text’s genre
engines.row_unit: one row per sequence, perspective or temporal move

engines.use_when: separate the author’s voice from quotations and attributed positions
engines.yields: speaker and quotation tables with attribution chains
engines.row_unit: one row per attributed passage

engines.use_when: trace each claim to its immediate attribution and mark upstream sources that were not supplied
engines.yields: claim provenance and access limits
engines.row_unit: one row per claim and its attributed source

engines.use_when: find the examples a text uses and distinguish their argumentative roles and limits
engines.yields: example inventory and use table
engines.row_unit: one row per example or argumentative use

groups.title: Count and date
groups.purpose: the numbers and the sequence of events as the sources give them, with what each can carry

engines.use_when: you will cite the sources' numbers and need to know what each one is (target, estimate, observation), over what base and period, what claim it carries, and which comparisons hold
engines.yields: quantity ledger (value · unit · of what · period · status · source · claim carried), comparisons with what differs, the figures the argument lacks
engines.row_unit: one row per quantity
engines.fit_note: needs a text with numbers; on a purely conceptual paper it returns a short inventory and says so

engines.use_when: you need the sequence of events as the sources report it and must know which causal links the sources actually support
engines.yields: timeline (event · date · precision · actor · source), causal links (cause → effect · type · asserted or implied · support), coverage and gaps
engines.row_unit: one row per event or link
engines.fit_note: needs dated reporting; a gap is reported as a gap, never as concealment

engines.use_when: inventory the rules a document reports and distinguish their status from observed responses
engines.yields: dated rule inventory and response table
engines.row_unit: one row per reported rule or response

engines.use_when: test where an account divides history into periods and what alternative cuts change
engines.yields: period boundary audit and alternatives
engines.row_unit: one row per boundary or alternative period

excluded.why: presumes a selected source thinker and a subject author (Anxiety-of-Influence workflow); no such structure in a corpus dossier
